sections.shortTitle: Representation of the People Fourth Amendment Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Short title and commencement

ORDINANCE CXII OF 1996
ORDINANCE CXII OF 1996
REPRESENTATION OF THE PEOPLE (FOURTH
AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1996
An Ordinance further to amend the
Representation of the People Act, 1976.
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part 1,
5th December, 1996]
No‑F.2(1)/96‑Pub., dated 5‑12‑1996.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:
Whereas it is expedient further to amend the
Representation of the People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976), for the purposes
hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the National Assembly is not in
session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it
necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers
conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
1. Short
title and commencement. ‑‑‑(I) This Ordinance may be called the
Representation of the People (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1996.
(2) It shall come into force at once.

ORDINANCE CXII OF 1996
ORDINANCE CXII OF 1996
REPRESENTATION OF THE PEOPLE (FOURTH

An Ordinance further to amend the
Representation of the People Act, 1976.
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part 1,
5th December, 1996]
No‑F.2(1)/96‑Pub., dated 5‑12‑1996.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:
Whereas it is expedient further to amend the
Representation of the People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976), for the purposes
hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the National Assembly is not in
session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it
necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers
conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
10. Insertion of new section, Act LXXXV of
1976.‑‑In
the said Act, after section 42, amended as aforesaid, the following new section
shall be inserted, namely:‑‑
"42A. Yearly submission of statements
of assets and liabilities (1) Every member shall, on a form as prescribed
under clause (viii) of subsection (2) of section 12, submit a statement of
assets and liabilities of his own, his spouse and dependents annually to the
Commission by the thirtieth day of September each year.
(2) The statements of assets and liabilities
submitted under subsection (1) shall be published in the official Gazette and
copies thereof can be obtained on payment of prescribed fee.
(3) The Commissioner shall, by the fifteenth
day of October each year, notify the names of the members who fail to file
statements of assets and liabilities within the period specified in subsection
(1) and by an order, direct that such member shall cease to function till such
statement is submitted.
(4) Where a member submits the statement of
assets and liabilities under subsection (1) which is found to be false in
material particulars, he may be proceeded under section 82 for committing the
offence of corrupt practice.".

Whereas it is expedient further to amend the

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers
conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
11. Insertion of new sections, Act LXXXV of
1976.‑‑In
the said Act, in Chapter VI, after section 47‑A, the following new
sections shall be inserted; namely:‑‑
"48. Definition.‑‑For
the purpose of this Act, "election expenses" means any expenditure
incurred before, during and after an election or payment made, whether by way
of gift, loan, advance, deposit or otherwise, for the arrangement conduct or
benefit of, or in connection with or incidental to, the election of a
candidate, including the expenditure on account of issuing circulars or
publications, but does not include the deposit made under section 13.
49. Restriction on election expenses.‑‑(1)
No' person other than the candidate `shall incur any election expenses of such
candidate:
Provided that where any person, incurs any
election expenses for such candidate, whether for stationery, postage,
telegrams, advertisements or for any other item whatsoever, such expenses shall
be deemed to be the election expenses incurred by the candidate himself.
(2) The election expenses of a contesting
candidate shall not exceed, in the case of an election to a seat in the
National Assembly, one million rupees and, in the case of an‑election to
a seat in a Provincial Assembly, six hundred thousand rupees.
(3) A candidate shall, by a bill stating the
particulars and by a receipt, vouch for every payment made in respect of
election expenses except where the amount is less than five hundred rupees.
50. Return of
election expenses. ‑‑(1) Every contesting candidate, other than the
returned candidate, shall, within thirty days after the publication of the name
of the returned candidate, submit to the Returning Officer a return of election
expenses in the prescribed form containing‑‑
(a) a statement of all payments made by him
together with all bills and receipts;
(b) a statement of all disputed claims;
(c) a statement of all unpaid claims, if any;
and
(d) a statement of all moneys, securities or
equivalent of money received from, or spent, by any person for the benefit of
the contesting candidate, specifying the name of every such person.
(2) The return submitted under subsection (1)
shall be accompanied by an affidavit in the prescribed form sworn by the
contesting candidate.
51. Inspection of returns, etc. ‑‑(1)
The return and documents submitted under section 50 shall be kept by the
Returning Officer in his office or at such other convenient place as he may think
fit and shall, during one year from the date of their receipt by him, be open
to inspection by any person on payment of the prescribed fee.
(2) The Returning Officer shall, or an
application made in this behalf and payment of the prescribed fee, give any
person copies of any return or document kept under subsection (1) or of any
part tliereof. "

sections.shortTitle: Representation of the People Fourth Amendment Ordinance 1996
sections.description:
Insertion of new sections 83A, 83B, Act LXXXV of 1976

ORDINANCE CXII OF 1996
ORDINANCE CXII OF 1996
REPRESENTATION OF THE PEOPLE (FOURTH
AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1996
An Ordinance further to amend the
Representation of the People Act, 1976.
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part 1,
5th December, 1996]
No‑F.2(1)/96‑Pub., dated 5‑12‑1996.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:
Whereas it is expedient further to amend the
Representation of the People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976), for the purposes
hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the National Assembly is not in
session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it
necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers
conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
16. Insertion of new sections 83A, 83B, Act
LXXXV of 1976.‑‑In
the said Act, after section 83, the following new sections shall be inserted,
namely:‑‑
"83A. Prohibition of affixing hoardings,
etc.‑‑(1) No person or a political party shall affix hoardings,
posters or banners of any size or cause wall chalking as a part of election
campaign of a candidate:
(2) No person or a political party shall hoist
or fix party's flags on any public property or at any public place; nor shall
use loudspeaker for election campaign except at the election meetings.
(3) The Deputy Commissioner and the concerned
Returning Officer shall be responsible for the effective implementation of the
provisions of sub sections (1) and (2).
(4) The contravention of the provisions of
subsections (1) and (2) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not
exceeding one year, or with fine, or with both.
83B. Election campaign by political parties.‑‑(1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in section 83A, a political party may, at
the national level, publish or broadcast or cause to be published or broadcast
advertisements as a part of its election campaign:
Provided that the total expenses of such
publication, broadcast or advertisement shall not exceed thirty million rupees.
(2) Every political party shall, within thirty
days of poll, submit to Commissioner the accounts‑of its election
receipts and expenditure duly signed by the head of the political party.
(3) Any party contravening the provisions of
subsection (1) shall be liable to fine by the Commissioner twice the amount in
excess of thirty million rupees. "
(4) Where a political party fails to submit the
accounts of its election receipts and expenditure, the Commission may impose
such fine as it may deem fit.
Explanation.‑‑For the purpose of
this section, "election receipts" shall include contributions,
donations, loans, party ticket fees and gifts, in cash or kind. "
